newsitem.title: FRANCE: Trinidad LNG project on course for May '99 startup.
newsitem.headline: Trinidad LNG project on course for May '99 startup.

text.p: The Atlantic LNG project to produce liquefied natural gas in Trinidad and Tobago is set for start-up in May 1999, an industry conference heard on Friday.

Gordon Shearer, president of operator Cabot LNG Corp, said that the Atlantic LNG project is one of several due on stream at around the same time. He even added that his company has a bet of two bottles of champagne with Nigeria LNG Ltd on who will ship gas first.
The two biggest shareholders in the project are Amoco Corp with 34 percent and British Gas with 26 percent. Amoco only discovered the project's largest field after work had already started.
Cabot is aiming to produce nearly four billion cubic metres a year of LNG.

Shearer said that Cabot had decided on Trinidad because of the small scale of the project, strong government support, and the fact that the industry there is well established. Trinidad has been producing oil for 100 years and gas for 25 years, he said.
They were also sure of selling the LNG, as the project will supply a specific buyer in the northeast United States.

Shearer believes Trinidad's location gives the Atlantic LNG project a key advantage over whether projects. "We are able to arbitrage between North America and Europe depending on gas prices, and we intend to do so," he said.
